labels.text: Change a schedule's name, description, prompt, model, cron expression or time zone.
IANA time zone the cron expression is read in. Defaults to this machine's.

S42.04.needs: a signed-in account (schedules run in AGI cloud)
S42.04.note: The words "briefing" and "delivery" do not appear in apps/cli; the nearest feature is scheduled agent runs with a cron expression and timezone, so the tester should treat a schedule as the briefing.
steps: Run `agi schedules create --name "Morning briefing" --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt "Summarize my day" --timezone America/New_York`.
Note the id the command prints.
Run `agi schedules list` and check that the cadence and timezone shown match the new zone (compare with Expected: the user sets the delivery time and timezone).
S42.04.where: Type `agi schedules create --name <name> --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt <text> --timezone <IANA zone>` to set the time and zone, or `agi schedules edit <id or exact name> --timezone <IANA zone>` to change them later. Check with `agi schedules list`.

labels.text: Stop a schedule from firing until it is resumed.
Let a paused schedule fire again.

S42.15.needs: a signed-in account and at least one existing schedule (create one with `agi schedules create` first)
S42.15.note: The word "briefing" does not appear in apps/cli; pause and resume apply to schedules.
steps: Run `agi schedules list` and note the id and status of a schedule.
Run `agi schedules pause <id or exact name>`.
Run `agi schedules list` and check that the schedule shows as paused (not active).
Run `agi schedules resume <id or exact name>`, then `agi schedules list` again, and check it is active. Compare with Expected: the user can pause and resume briefings.
S42.15.where: Type `agi schedules pause <id or exact name>` and `agi schedules resume <id or exact name>`. Check status with `agi schedules list`.

labels.text: Bell when a long turn finishes
Ring the terminal bell when a long turn finishes?

S42.17.needs: a terminal that plays a bell sound, and a long-running chat request
S42.17.note: Only a foreground chat turn of 10 seconds or more rings the bell (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs); no completion notice for scheduled runs was found, and background runs are shown only through `agi background list`, `/threads` and `/gather`, so this may not match Expected.
steps: Type `/config set bell true` and press Enter.
Type `/config get bell` and check that it reports true.
Send a chat request that takes at least 10 seconds, switch to another window, and listen for the terminal bell when the turn finishes.

Compare with Expected: the user is notified when background work (a scheduled run or agent task) completes. The bell covers only a foreground chat turn, so a scheduled run finishing should not ring it.
S42.17.where: Type `/config set bell true` in the chat, then `/config get bell` to check it. The bell itself is shown as "Bell when a long turn finishes" in `/config show`.
